# Native local asset evidence

The immutable reference is v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. Ignored collectors verify imported `local_models.py`, `local_qwen.py`, `local_gpu.py`, `config.py` and catalog resources against that commit before collecting observations. Maintained tests and asset installation are native Rust and require no reference implementation or interpreter.

| Fixture | Independent observations | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `released-local-assets.json` | Six-model catalog, both Qwen runtime manifests, 75 download/archive/readiness cases and 45 storage decisions | `a99e95731f964a941368bc5270ad51477f1c9c502e15e8f4c78036d8692873ac` |
| `released-pinned-runtimes.json` | 130 filesystem entries from actual pinned CPU and Vulkan archive installations | `1d5c198a1aee49f7f43880fd5c79fa46f9184d5c37dce50828845470f19293ec` |

All six existing model IDs, labels, offered/hidden choices, engines, quantization, RAM estimates, revisions, file names, lengths and hashes remain unchanged. Catalog resources are compiled into the native library. Existing model paths and revision/checksum markers remain readable. Readiness retains the released size/marker/executable checks rather than silently requiring another download. The existing `cuda` runtime key still selects the pinned Vulkan archive; its settings and storage name are preserved.

Twenty model and twelve runtime cases use genuine HTTPS requests through a private TLS CONNECT proxy, with separate native children, cleared inherited environments, synthetic public artifact bytes and private data roots. The comparison covers actual request method/host/path, declared sizes and SHA-256, redirects, HTTP failure, cancellation, ready-cache reuse, partial-file cleanup, retries and multifile failure. Progress values compare exact IEEE-754 bits; differing JSON exponent spellings are normalized without a numerical tolerance. The native branded User-Agent differs from the interpreter's injected header. Request header byte identity is not claimed.

The nonblocking download lock is held across runtime preparation and weights. A held-lock comparison uses the public native guard in the parent and observes refusal from another process; release allows another download. Mutable access to the guard serializes its installation phases so parallel futures cannot bypass the lock by sharing one job. Thirty-six model and nine runtime preflight decisions preserve the shared 5 GB budget, 100 MB temporary model headroom and 250 MB runtime budget, including exact boundary messages. The reference overrides only filesystem capacity measurements and witnesses accepted preflight through an actual HTTPS request. Native disk usage excludes symlinks and counts regular files, including hard links. Healthy large transfers have a thirty-second connection/read budget, with no overall thirty-second download deadline.

Seventeen archive cases observe containment, absolute/relative paths, links, special-file refusal, declared extraction budget, permissions, timestamps, malformed archives and cleanup. Twenty-six readiness cases cover all six models and both runtime devices with valid, stale, wrong-size, missing and nonexecutable inputs. Archive/OS/network failures use controlled native diagnostics rather than copying interpreter exception strings; these failures compare categories and filesystem outcomes. Exact controller error-display acceptance remains pending.

The explicitly executed pinned-runtime test downloads both unchanged `b11011` public archives into disposable storage through the production native installer. SHA-256 and exact declared lengths pass. Every extracted file's content hash, size and mode, every link target, and archive directory/file timestamps match the independently installed release: 130 entries and 127,217,268 stored bytes. Both executable/marker readiness checks pass. This establishes real artifact acceptance, not speech inference or GPU device availability. The network test is ignored by ordinary runs and must be invoked explicitly with `cargo test --locked -p mluva-providers --test local_assets actual_pinned_qwen_archives_match_released_installations -- --ignored --exact`.

Four ordinary asset tests pass, bringing the workspace to 102 ordinary passing native tests. Formatting and Clippy with warnings denied pass. Three isolated GTK tests, the installed-Codex test and this public-download test are excluded from the ordinary run and retain their explicitly executed evidence. Synthetic peers and collectors never ship; `asset-fixture-peer` must not be included by a blanket workspace install. No host model store, credentials, user content, audio device, settings or visible desktop were used or changed.

`install_model_files` is the weight phase after the caller prepares the selected runtime under the same guard. Complete provider coordination, local recognition, native ONNX CPU/GPU runtime provisioning, model unloading and settings/welcome integration remain required. The legacy ONNX GPU installer is not carried into this asset component. Complete app workflows, distribution, final Python removal and same-host performance acceptance remain pending. Installed app and widget remain v1.6.0.
